doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
title: Playing solo and on the Madisonville boat
summary: Billie worked with Mac but also solo; De De recalls the lake boat, its landings and its favourite number.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Were you playing with bands or solo? I was playing solo.

But I worked with Mac all through that. But I mean, we just go, see, we used to go. Palmeta. See, like with the human on, here comes the bookman, short man. You see, uh. Palmeta? That's all right, get it. You come here.
Get it on the air. That's a bowl. That's a bowl. And you have everything on the guard screen.

You know what was interesting was when the boat was coming into Madisonville, everything was quiet. You see, all of a sudden, the van would start flying full speed, and she'd make that landing, and all the people would come on just to walk around and see the boat and see the van and everything. Oh, man, we used to go out and catch one of them 65 cents chicken. I know. I mean, a very chicken too. 65 cents? You wanted to eat. Then they would punish you some drinks. That's right. Yeah, man. And then you'd come back to the boat, and then you'd go right on back over. Now, sometimes it would be 6 or 7 o'clock before the boat would die back. Well, I hope they tell you. But those, you didn't have much.

I used to get in here running by 9 o'clock. Let me get in here for 9 o'clock that night, see? And then I would leave them here and go down to the old folks' home, down to the luchards. And start playing that. And me diddy down there, see?
You know what was our favorite number? And see if I was not right. Is it true?
What they say about Dixie. I'm glad to hear you. That's my number was on the boat.
I'm glad to meet both of you. I'm glad to meet you, Mr. Brooks. So are you?
